transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

It is not faulty and you do not need to send it back. The 3 hours 39 minutes shown for the Eco 40-60 cycle is completely normal for this model. These programmes are designed to save energy by using lower water temperatures and longer wash times, which is why they take much longer than older machines or quick cycles. To be absolutely sure there isn't a heating issue (which would also make it take even longer), you can run a standard 60°C Cottons cycle next time. If the clothes come out warm at the end of that cycle, your machine is working perfectly.
Thanks. I'd rather not run a 60 wash just to test it though, I want to use the most efficient programme. Is there anything else I can check or do to shorten the Eco 40-60 time?

The Eco 40-60 programme is designed to be energy-efficient rather than fast, so the long duration is built-in and cannot be significantly shortened without changing the settings. However, you can reduce the time slightly by ensuring you don't overload the drum (the machine needs room to tumble), using liquid detergent which dissolves faster at lower temperatures, and making sure your household water pressure isn't unusually low, as a slow fill will extend the cycle. If you need a quicker wash occasionally, simply select a different programme like 'Cottons 40' or 'Mixes', but be aware these will use more energy than the Eco setting.
